subject.title: Stuck-session liveness monitor misclassifies healthy processing runs as stale during event-loop stalls

question: Should OpenClaw change the processing/no-activeWorkKind recovery policy now, or require live measurement proving healthy active runs can lose activity bookkeeping during event-loop stalls?
rationale: Current source shows the reported fallthrough, but tests and docs encode deliberate stale-processing recovery semantics and the report labels the healthy-run abort chain as likely rather than confirmed.

options.title: Require proof first
options.body: Keep this issue open for targeted live or deterministic evidence showing stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run on a healthy processing run before changing recovery semantics.

options.title: Patch classifier now
options.body: Approve a narrow classifier change for processing/no-activeWorkKind sessions, accepting the need to redesign stale-processing recovery tests.

options.title: Fold into active-run recovery
options.body: Treat this as a subcase of the broader false active-run abort policy tracked by related stuck-session recovery work.

recommendation.title: Require proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for targeted live or deterministic evidence showing stale_session_state and abort_embedded_run on a healthy processing run before changing recovery semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently changed orphaned stalled-lane recovery in this same policy area, making them the best available routing owner for the recovery semantics choice.
